title: Example: Politics as a Vocation
notes:
Some guiding questions I have in mind:
- What are the significant implications for what politics as a vocation entails?
- What is the core thesis that Max Weber wants the users to focus on?
- How does he define these key terms: politics, vocation, power, state?
- Why do people listen to the state and what purpose does the state serve for people?

***

- "Significance of political action in the whole way of life"(3) rather than a focus on his stance on any given contemporary issue of the day
- politics - broad concept but really about "any kind of *independent* leadership in action" (3)
- Insight: I never directly made the connection about how politics requires an element of "independence" for it to work effectively. This is constrast with say corporate leadership where a hierarchy requires everyone "reporting" to some degree (e.g, even CEO reports to board of directors, and board directors report to shareholders). Yes even politicians are "beholden" to their electorate, but their is an understanding that the politician will likely move in way that are not entirely in accordance / congruent with everything the electorate wants
- Also interesting that politics is seen so broadly that even "policy of a prudent wife who seeks to guide her"(3) falls under politics
- Weber focuses his discussion on politicis only on "leadership, or the influencing of the leadership, of a political association" (3) that he calls a state

cards.text: You contrast politics with corporate hierarchy, but I compare them myself later: shareholders are as little influential in management as a 'people' ruled by expert officials [p. 15]. Is political independence then partly an illusion?
cards.anchor: politics requires an element of "independence" for it to work effectively
